laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They can include long jail terms. Airports in Tanzania have technology and security for detecting illegal items, including drugs. This can be used to scan the baggage of transiting passengers.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: It's illegal to possess or access pornographic material.
laws.heading: Pornography

laws.rule: Same-sex activity is illegal in Tanzania. Authorities can jail you for up to 30 years. Authorities might subject you to an invasive examination. Security forces sometimes carry out arbitrary arrests and searches based on sexual orientation or gender identity. Interventions include: detentions interrogations alleged physical abuse Members of the LGBTQIA+ community and advocates can be targets for harassment. There are regular cases of harassment and arrests by authorities and intimidation by members of the public. LGBTQIA+ travellers should take precautions.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ laws

laws.rule: It's illegal to photograph military zones, weapons or personnel. Single-use plastic bags are banned, including in your luggage. You can face heavy fines and imprisonment for up to 7 days. Serious crimes, such as treason and murder, carry the death penalty. There's corporal punishment for some crimes. This includes rape or robbery with violence. Be aware of how you use social media, and what you post online. You need to comply with cybercrime laws.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Flying a drone in Tanzania without TCAA approval is illegal, including for personal or hobby use. Foreign visitors get the drone registered, the pilot registered and an operations permit before arriving, applying three to four weeks ahead. Drones are barred near military sites, State House, prisons and airports, and need special permission near government buildings, national parks and crowded places.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress and behaviour standards are conservative in Tanzania, especially in Zanzibar. Take care to be respectful and not offend. Avoid public displays of affection. If you're a woman, don't wear shorts or sleeveless tops outside tourist resorts. The Tanzanian Embassy's useful information covers modest dress. In Zanzibar's Stone Town, swimwear is for beaches only.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: TCAA says foreign individuals and companies may operate drones if they get TCAA permits before arriving: register the drone, register the pilot as operator and apply for an operations permit (3 to 4 weeks ahead). Every flight needs a permit, recreational included, and third-party insurance is mandatory.

items.text: Not yet checked: no public TCAA directory of drone operators was found on the pages read.
A permit is required for every drone operation, including recreational use, and permits are usually tied to specific locations. Third-party liability insurance is mandatory when registering a drone.

TCAA's FAQ says foreigners can operate drones if they obtain TCAA permits before arriving: non-residents register the drone, register the pilot as operator and apply for an operations permit through drones@tcaa.go.tz. Lead time is stated as three weeks, one month, or three to four weeks on different pages. Non-resident operations permits are listed at USD 10 a day for lighter drones (about A$14.20 at the RBA rate of 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040), rising with weight; the pages do not fully match, so confirm fees.
